findings.title: Fail closed after any reservation-bound overrun
findings.body: The packet residual boundary requires observed actual above bounds to remain recorded and fail closed for further reservation. settle_budget only releases bounds and adds actuals; reserve_budget checks aggregate root limits without remembering a reservation-bound violation. With root token limit1000, bound100 and verified actual101, the actual is retained but the next bound100 reservation is accepted. This continues using an upper-bound configuration already demonstrated to be unenforceable. Both existing overrun tests exceed the entire root limit (unit tokens999, database tokens2000), so they only prove ordinary aggregate exhaustion. The call_ledger contract narrows the packet to an overdrawn root, and the selected PASS evidence does not establish the packet requirement.
findings.required_change: Persist an accounting-only fail-closed overrun basis in the same settlement transaction and deny new reservations on that root after any enforced actual exceeds its reservation bound; retain all actual amounts and immutable receipt evidence without changing intent/attempt/authorization state. Preserve the denial through join/revision/takeover and replay. Update the contract to the packet semantics and add PU plus migrated PostgreSQL service assertions for bound overrun below root limits, including normal in-bound settlement and atomic rollback controls.
findings.independent_reproduction: Read-only in-memory invocation of actual settle_budget/reserve_budget using limits calls3/tokens1000/tools10, reserved calls1/tokens100/tools1, actual calls1/tokens101/tools1: settlement records101; subsequent bounds calls1/tokens100/tools1 succeeds. No DB, Docker, implementation or evidence mutation used.

findings.title: Bind all prepared S31 dispatch and configuration fields
findings.body: The new prepared reservation guard compares ID, payload, status, revision and operation slot, but omits dispatch_owner, dispatch_fence and config_fingerprint. prepare_ledger_reservation captures owner/fence and the accounting identity; a restricted ReserveCall callback can nevertheless insert different column values. The existing live-chain predicate checks intent/attempt only, and completion checks do not compare these dispatch/config fields. permit_dispatch subsequently trusts the stored dispatch_fence, so a forged future fence can make a reservation dispatchable after a later takeover instead of binding it to the reservation-time authority. This violates the declared exact reservation identity/bounds/fence guard and permits disagreement between S31 columns and accounting evidence. Current negative callbacks corrupt only typed_payload and miss this case.
findings.required_change: Compare the complete prepared subject/intent/attempt/operation/accounting/configuration/dispatch-owner/fence chain at S31 insertion, preserving legacy owner compatibility only where the packet permits it. Add migrated PostgreSQL negative callbacks that independently alter owner, fence, config fingerprint and parent chain; assert GuardRequired and complete S27/S31/S32/S02/S03/S04 rollback. Verify an obsolete reservation cannot gain permission by a fabricated future fence.
findings.independent_reproduction: Read-only in-memory call to actual RestrictedSqlSession._require_insert_bindings(S31, values), with prepared owner-real/fence1/config-real and values owner-invented/fence2/config-invented, returned without GuardRequired. This is guard reproduction, not migrated PostgreSQL contender evidence.
